settings.description: The value the Anthropic adapter sends in the anthropic-version header. Gateways that speak the Messages API, such as Ollama and LiteLLM, expect this one.

How many times the Anthropic adapter sends a call again when it failed before any of the reply arrived and the failure may pass: a rate limit, a busy provider, or an endpoint that could not be reached. Zero means never.
How long the Anthropic adapter waits before its first retry. Each later wait is twice the one before.
The longest the Anthropic adapter waits before a retry. When the provider asks for a longer wait, the call fails at once so another model can be tried.
How long an endpoint that speaks the Anthropic Messages API may take to begin its answer. A local model that has to be loaded first needs the time. Zero means no limit.
How long a reply from the Anthropic adapter's endpoint may send nothing before the call is given up. Zero means no limit.
Whether the Anthropic adapter marks the end of the system blocks and of the last message so the provider can cache what comes before.

The provider model names, separated by commas, that are asked for thinking as a token budget. A name ending in * matches by its start. Every other model is asked for adaptive thinking, where the model decides how much to think.
How many characters the fake provider sends in each piece of a streamed reply. Zero sends each block in one piece.
How long the fake provider waits before each piece of a streamed reply, so a chat in the test tenant streams at a speed a person can watch. Tests use no wait.
How many numbers each vector the fake provider makes holds, when a registry entry on the fake adapter is an embedding model, from 1 to 65536. Zero makes the fake make no vectors.
The most models one person's registry may hold. Adding one more is refused.
How many characters of text count as one token when Keystone estimates a call's size because the provider offers no count. Lower counts more tokens, which is the safe side.
The safety margin added to an estimated token count, as a percentage of it. A provider's own count gets no margin.
Tokens counted for each message in an estimate, for its role and framing, on top of its content.
Tokens counted for each tool offered in an estimate, on top of its name, description and schema.
Tokens counted for each image in an estimate, whatever its size.
Tokens counted in an estimate for a file that is named by reference, whose size the estimate cannot see.
How many times the Responses adapter sends a call again when it failed before any of the reply arrived and the failure is one that may pass. Zero sends each call once.
How long the Responses adapter waits before its first retry. The wait doubles with each retry.
The longest the Responses adapter waits before a retry. When the provider asks for a longer wait, the call fails at once so another model can be tried.
How long the Responses adapter waits for a reply to begin before it gives up on the call.
How long a streamed reply through the Responses adapter may send nothing before it is given up on.
The thinking budget, in tokens, from which the Responses adapter asks for medium reasoning effort. A smaller budget asks for low.
The thinking budget, in tokens, from which the Responses adapter asks for high reasoning effort.
How long the Chat Completions adapter waits to connect to an endpoint, and again to finish the TLS handshake.
How long the Chat Completions adapter waits for an endpoint to start its answer. A local model that is still loading needs the time.
How long the Chat Completions adapter waits between two pieces of a streamed reply before it ends the call.
How many times the Chat Completions adapter sends one call at most, when the endpoint is busy or cannot be reached. One means no retry.
How long the Chat Completions adapter waits before it sends a call again. The wait doubles with each attempt.
The registry name of the model that writes summaries of a chat. Empty, or a name that is not in the registry, uses the chat's own model.
The registry name of the model that runs the memory pass after a turn. Empty, or a name that is not in the registry, uses the chat's own model.
The registry name of the model that turns text into vectors. It must have the embedding capability.
Registry names, separated by commas, of the models to try in order when the model a call was meant for fails before any of its reply arrived. Empty means a failed call is not sent to another model.
The most other models one call is sent to after the first one failed. Zero means none.
The most one person may spend in a calendar month, in US dollars, on models that are not local. A call that could take the month past it is not sent. Zero stops every call that costs anything.
The share of the monthly cap, in percent, at which Keystone starts to warn that the cap is near.
The longest the Chat Completions adapter waits between two attempts, whatever the endpoint asks for.
